His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾. Regarding this there are four opinions:

Third: It is the believers. This was said by al-Hasan, and the "clear evidence" is the miracle (mu'jizah) of the Messenger.

Fourth: It is the religion (al-din). This was said by al-Kalbi.

One: Their worship of idols. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Second: Their polytheism (shirk). This was said by Qatadah. Regarding who is meant here there are two opinions:

One: They are all the polytheists.

(p-297) Second: They are the twelve men of Quraysh.

Regarding who made it attractive to them there are two opinions:

One: Satan.

Second: Their own souls.

﴿And they followed their desires﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One: It is a description of those for whom the evil of their deeds has been made attractive.

Second: They are the hypocrites. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who believe say, "If only a surah were sent down!"﴾ When the revelation of the Qur'an was delayed, the believers longed for it and wished for it, so that they might know the commands of God and the acts of worship He prescribed for them.

﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ In one reading, attributed to Ibn Mas'ud: "But when a new surah is sent down." Regarding the "decisive" (muhkamah) surah there are two opinions:

One: it is the surah in which lawful and unlawful matters are mentioned. This was said by Ibn Ziyad al-Naqqash.

(p-301) The second: it is the surah in which fighting is mentioned, for it is the most severe part of the Qur'an against the hypocrites. This was said by Qatadah.

It may also be understood, as a third possibility, that it is the surah containing texts that were not later abrogated (naskh) and about which no interpretation (ta'wil) differs.

﴿And you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ They are the hypocrites, because their hearts are like a sick heart through doubt.

When a decisive surah is sent down, the believers rejoice at it and hasten to act upon what is in it, while the hypocrites are distressed and look at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ﴿with the look of one who has fainted from death﴾, out of grief over it and fear of it.

﴿So woe to them﴾ On this there are two views:

One: it is a threat, as if He said: "Punishment is more fitting for them." This was said by Qatadah.

The second: "Woe to them" means: ﴿obedience and fair speech﴾ would have been better for them than to recoil from the obligation of jihad upon them. This was said by al-Hasan.

There is also a third view: that His saying ﴿obedience and fair speech﴾ is a report from God about them before the obligation of jihad was imposed on them. This was mentioned by Ibn 'Isa.

Obedience (taah) is obedience to God and His Messenger in commands and prohibitions.

Regarding "fair speech" (qawl ma'ruf) there are two views:

One: it is truthfulness and acceptance.

The second: it is responding by hearing and obeying.

﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾ meaning: when the matter of fighting becomes serious.

﴿Then if they had been true to God﴾ in their deeds ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ than their hypocrisy.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿Would you, if you turned away, then cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ On this there are four views:

One: "Would you, if you were given charge of the affairs of the community, cause corruption on the earth through injustice." This was said by al-Kalbi.

(p-302) The second: "Would you, if you were given judgeship and made judges, cause corruption on the earth by taking bribes." This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The third: "Would you, if you turned away from the Book of God, cause corruption on the earth by shedding forbidden blood." This was said by Qatadah, and [the rest of the verse, "and sever your ties of kinship"] is also from him.

The fourth: "Would you, if you turned away from obedience, cause corruption on the earth through sins and severing ties of kinship." This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Regarding this verse there are three opinions:

One: that it refers to the hypocrites, and this is the apparent meaning.

The second: that it refers to the Quraysh, said by Abu Hayyan.

The third: that it was revealed concerning the Kharijites, said by Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani.

﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ In one reading, attributed to Ibn Mas'ud: "But when a new surah is sent down." Regarding the "decisive" (muhkamah) surah there are two opinions:

One: it is the surah in which lawful and unlawful matters are mentioned. This was said by Ibn Ziyad al-Naqqash.

(p-301) The second: it is the surah in which fighting is mentioned, for it is the most severe part of the Qur'an against the hypocrites. This was said by Qatadah.

It may also be understood, as a third possibility, that it is the surah containing texts that were not later abrogated (naskh) and about which no interpretation (ta'wil) differs.

﴿And you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ They are the hypocrites, because their hearts are like a sick heart through doubt.

When a decisive surah is sent down, the believers rejoice at it and hasten to act upon what is in it, while the hypocrites are distressed and look at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ﴿with the look of one who has fainted from death﴾, out of grief over it and fear of it.

﴿So woe to them﴾ On this there are two views:

One: it is a threat, as if He said: "Punishment is more fitting for them." This was said by Qatadah.

The second: "Woe to them" means: ﴿obedience and fair speech﴾ would have been better for them than to recoil from the obligation of jihad upon them. This was said by al-Hasan.

There is also a third view: that His saying ﴿obedience and fair speech﴾ is a report from God about them before the obligation of jihad was imposed on them. This was mentioned by Ibn 'Isa.

Obedience (taah) is obedience to God and His Messenger in commands and prohibitions.

Regarding "fair speech" (qawl ma'ruf) there are two views:

One: it is truthfulness and acceptance.

The second: it is responding by hearing and obeying.

﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾ meaning: when the matter of fighting becomes serious.

﴿Then if they had been true to God﴾ in their deeds ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ than their hypocrisy.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿Would you, if you turned away, then cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ On this there are four views:

One: "Would you, if you were given charge of the affairs of the community, cause corruption on the earth through injustice." This was said by al-Kalbi.

(p-302) The second: "Would you, if you were given judgeship and made judges, cause corruption on the earth by taking bribes." This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The third: "Would you, if you turned away from the Book of God, cause corruption on the earth by shedding forbidden blood." This was said by Qatadah, and [the rest of the verse, "and sever your ties of kinship"] is also from him.

The fourth: "Would you, if you turned away from obedience, cause corruption on the earth through sins and severing ties of kinship." This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Regarding this verse there are three opinions:

One: that it refers to the hypocrites, and this is the apparent meaning.

The second: that it refers to the Quraysh, said by Abu Hayyan.

The third: that it was revealed concerning the Kharijites, said by Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 47, verse 24–28:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them...﴾ Concerning them there are two opinions:

The first: they are the Jews, who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) after they had known from the Torah that he was a Prophet. This was said by Qatadah and Ibn Juraij.

The second: they are the hypocrites, who held back from fighting after they had known it from the Qur'an. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿Satan made it seem fair to them﴾. Concerning this there are two meanings (p-303):
The first: he granted them what they asked for. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

The second: he made their misdeeds appear attractive to them. This was said by al-Hasan.

﴿And he gave them respite﴾. Concerning this there are two meanings:

The first: he gave them time. This was said by al-Kalbi and Muqatil. According to this, Allah Most High is the One who gives them respite, in delaying their punishment.

The second meaning: that the sense of "amla lahum" is that he extended hope for them, that is, he lengthened their hopes. According to this, there are two views:

The first: that Allah Most High is the One who extended hope for them. This was said by al-Farra' and al-Mufaddal.

The second: that Satan is the one who extended their hopes by procrastination (tasweef). This was said by al-Hasan.

﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down: "We will obey you in part of the matter."﴾ Concerning the speaker of this there are two opinions:

The first: they are the Jews, who said to the hypocrites, "We will obey you in part of the matter." Concerning what they intended by this there are two meanings:

The first: "We will obey you in not believing anything of his speech." This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: "We will obey you in concealing what we know of his prophethood." This was said by Ibn Juraij.

The second opinion: they are the hypocrites, who said to the Jews, "We will obey you in part of the matter." Concerning what they intended by this there are three meanings:

The first: "We will obey you in refraining from fighting, out of hatred for Muhammad (ﷺ), and in sitting back from supporting him." This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: "We will obey you in inclining towards you and aiding you against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

The third: "We will obey you in apostasy after faith."

﴿And Allah knows their secret conferring﴾. This may have two meanings:

The first: what some of them whispered to others of this saying.

The second: what they concealed within themselves of this belief.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ This may have two meanings:

The first: with fighting in support of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The second: with the seizing of souls at death.

(p-304) ﴿Striking their faces and their backs﴾. This may have two meanings:

The first: they strike their faces in fighting when pursued, and their backs when fleeing.

The second: they strike their faces at death with the pages of their disbelief, and their backs on the Day of Resurrection when they are driven to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 47, verse 29–31:

His words, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring out their malice?﴾ On this there are two views:

The first: doubt. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second: hypocrisy. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

﴿That Allah will not bring out their malice (adghan)﴾. On this there are four views:

The first: their deceit (ghishsh). This is the view of al-Suddi.

The second: their envy (hasad). This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

The third: their rancour (hiqd). This is the view of Ibn Isa.

The fourth: their hostility (ʿudwan). This is the view of Qutrub, who recited:

"Say to the son of Hind: what did you intend by speech that displeased the friend and pleased the holders of rancour?"

His words, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And you will surely recognise them in the tone of their speech (lahn al-qawl)﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: in the falsehood of their speech. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

The second: in the import (fahwa) of their words. Lahn means taking speech away from its direction, derived from lahn in i'rab (grammatical inflection, ʿIrab: the grammatical case endings of Arabic), which means departing from correctness. From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed you bring your disputes before me, and one of you may be more eloquent (alhan) in his argument," meaning he takes it in various directions because of his skill in turning speech.

Marar al-Asadi said:

"You have spoken a tone in which there is deceit, and your aversion has made me suspicious, [as you] adorn the informers and the enemies."

Al-Kalbi said: After its revelation, no hypocrite spoke in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ without being recognised by him.

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: the fighters in the way of Allah.

The second: those who renounce the world.

﴿And the patient﴾. On this there are two views:

The first: in jihad.

The second: in regard to the world.

﴿And We will test your reports (akhbar)﴾. This may bear two meanings:

The first: We will test your secrets.

The second: what you undertake of your actions.

The second: hypocrisy. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

The first: their deceit (ghishsh). This is the view of al-Suddi.

The first: in jihad.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He does not ask you for your wealth﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: He does not ask you for your wealth for His own sake.

Second: He does not ask you for all of your wealth in zakat, but only part of it.

Third: He does not ask you for your wealth, but rather asks you for His own wealth, because it is His and He is the one who bestows it by giving it to you.

﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: al-ihfa' (pressing, insisting) means taking all of it. This was said by Ibn Zayd and Qutrub.

Second: it means persistent urging and repeated asking, derived from al-hafa' (going barefoot, walking without sandals). This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

Third: the meaning of ﴿yuhfikum﴾ is that He finds you, so ﴿you would be stingy﴾. This was said by Ibn 'Uyayna.

﴿And He would bring forth your grudges﴾ (al-adghan, inner resentments). It may carry two meanings:

One: by your refusal, He brings forth what you have concealed of your enmity.

Two: at the time of being asked, you show what you have concealed of your hostility.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: "if you turn away" from My Book. This was said by Qatada.

Second: from My obedience. This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Third: from the charity you have been commanded to give. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Fourth: from this matter, so that you do not accept it. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿He will substitute a people other than you﴾. Regarding this there are three sayings:

First: they are the people of Yemen, who are the Helpers (al-Ansar). This was said by Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd.

Second: they are the Persians.

Abu Hurayra narrated that he said: When the verse ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾ was revealed, "Salman was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: O Messenger of Allah, who are these people whom, if we turn away, will be substituted in our place? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck Salman's shoulder and said: 'This man and his people. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if faith were suspended from al-Thurayya (the Pleiades), men from the sons of Persia would attain it.'"

Third: they are whoever among the rest of mankind He wills. This was said by Mujahid.

﴿Then they will not be like you﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

One: meaning in stinginess with spending in the way of Allah. This was said by al-Tabari.

Two: in disobedience and abandoning obedience.

It is related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari that "when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rejoiced at it and said: 'It is dearer to me than the world.'"
